parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Rust 2021, std-only, byte-identical CLI behavior, Cargo project placement, test16.rs entry point, and black-box use of the reference executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent probed the reference binary, delegated implementation to one coder child, then delegated read-only differential verification across six children with distinct input categories.
parallel.implementation: The coder child wrote Cargo.toml, test16.rs, and url_parser.rs, fixed no-scheme and query-fragment ordering mismatches found by probes and fuzzing, and rebuilt both cargo and rustc binaries.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Implementation was placed directly in /output with the required executable and Cargo files; parent consumed the child summary and ran spot checks before launching verification.
parallel.verification: Parent spot-checked corrected semantics, then five verifier children returned zero-mismatch reports across delimiter, port, host, scheme, and random fuzz categories; one structured-valid verifier was interrupted mid-run.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official correctness defect remained and the evaluator passed 40/40; process-wise the run timed out with one verifier aborted and no ordinary final parent answer.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, byte-identical CLI, Cargo project, test16.rs, and black-box probing requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent owned probing, implementation, integration, build, verification, and final reporting without delegation or shared ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote Cargo.toml plus url_parser/mod.rs, parser.rs, validators.rs, and test16.rs, then fixed an import issue to compile under Rust 2021.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial agent assembled the complete modular project in /output, produced the direct test16 executable and release build, and listed the delivered files.
serial.verification: It ran fixed cases, random fuzz, structured URL-shaped fuzz, no-argument checking, and release-binary example checks, all reporting zero differences from the reference executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task work is visible; the run completed normally, produced a final response, and passed the official 40/40 evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same C++ source, examples, Rust 2021, std-only, black-box, /output, and test16.rs requirements and used probes to refine behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial read the same prompt and also reconstructed the black-box URL behavior before writing a std-only Cargo project.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference affected correctness; both followed the prompt and resolved binary behavior where the prompt examples were incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent owned exploration and orchestration, delegated implementation to agent-0, and delegated six separate verification categories to the swarm.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all stages under one main agent and used a todo list to track probing, writing, compiling, and testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed implementation and verification across children, whereas serial performed the same pipeline locally; both had a clear implementation owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child received the task and returned concrete files, build results, and behavior corrections; verifier prompts shared the fixed executable path and reference path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained all probing findings in the same trajectory and encoded them into modular parser and validator files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoff boundaries but did not lose a known requirement or interface; the only problematic boundary was verifier lifecycle timing, not context transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation moved through child-generated single-file url_parser.rs, fixed observed mismatches for no-scheme and pre-query cut ordering, and achieved zero-mismatch local probes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the parser in separate url_parser modules, encountered an import compile error, fixed it, and then verified fixed/random/structured behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The code organization differed, but both implemented the same behavior and produced an accepted binary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retrieved agent-0's completed implementation result, but the later verification swarm ended with five completed verifier children and one aborted verifier after a turn cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it ran local verification commands and reached an ordinary final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material lifecycle difference is parallel's cancelled verifier result, while serial had no comparable child result to lose or interrupt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The coder child wrote the final project files and verifier children only read the produced /output/test16 binary; no cross-agent write collision or overwrite is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The single serial agent wrote and edited the project files itself, then listed the final project layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared workspace reads by verifier children but no realized contamination or write collision; serial avoided shared-state coordination entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had agent-0 probes/fuzz passing and five completed verifier reports with zero mismatches, then passed the official 40-case evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran fixed cases, random fuzz, structured fuzz, release examples, no-arg checking, and passed the same official evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had strong acceptance evidence, but parallel's verification was broader and distributed while one verifier was aborted; serial's verification was smaller but completed before final answer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used seven subagents, 1.16M tokens, and exhausted the process budget; status reports timed_out true even though artifact validation and evaluation succeeded.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, 950k tokens, completed in 759 agent seconds with 1638 seconds of budget remaining, and ended normally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget and timed out during distributed verification, while serial closed cleanly after local verification; this did not change the official pass outcome.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The mounted pair is not discordant under the current completed cell/status.json evaluations: both parallel and serial passed all 40 official testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is process shape and closure: parallel delegated implementation and verification, got a correct artifact, but timed out with one verifier aborted; serial performed the work locally and completed normally. The cancelled verifier is an adverse coordination episode, not an outcome-differential cause.
parallel_contributors: Delegated implementation found and fixed black-box parser edge cases before verification.
Distributed verifier children added broad zero-mismatch evidence, although one verifier was aborted.
serial_contributors: Single-agent continuity kept probing, implementation, tests, and final reporting in one context.
Serial completed local verification and final response without exhausting the process budget.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered a single url_parser.rs module while serial delivered url_parser/mod.rs, parser.rs, and validators.rs; both organizations passed official evaluation.
Serial briefly hit and fixed a Rust module import issue; parallel child instead fixed behavior mismatches found during fuzzing.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is adverse process evidence only

The parent did initial probing before delegation, but productive implementation was not blocked behind a failed or delaying mandatory preflight that left implementation unfinished.

The indispensable implementation path was not starved; agent-0 completed and verified the implementation before the later verifier cancellation.

Although the run timed out during a six-child verification swarm, the direct retained event is an explicit active-child cancellation and the artifact had already passed local checks; no separate collective fan-out episode left required implementation undone.

The implementation child received the known Rust, std-only, output-placement, black-box probing, and verification requirements; no omitted known requirement made its work unusable.

No known finding is shown disappearing across a handoff; the parent used the implementation child summary to spot-check corrected behavior.
Returned child summaries were long but decision-structured and consumed; the parent spot-checked implementation and launched targeted verification.
No child or parent consumed a superseded workspace or obsolete requirement state; later verification used the current /output/test16 executable.
Verifier handoffs were consistent zero-mismatch reports except the aborted verifier; there were no conflicting reports requiring adjudication.

The parent did not make an unsupported final completion decision; official evaluator evidence confirms success, and the retained issue is timeout during verification rather than an unsupported acceptance claim.
There was no replacement or retry of a failed child without inherited findings; the run used one implementation child and one verification swarm.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent launched a verification swarm, and active verifier agent-1 was cancelled while running its next slice before finalizing its assigned structured-valid-URL check; the aggregate result reported five completed children and one aborted child.
candidates.realized_consequence: Structured-valid-URL verification stopped before completion and the parent ended by timeout with an aborted verifier instead of a normal final closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The verifier workload was broad, but the complete implementation already existed and officially passed; the directly observed boundary is the cancellation of an active child, not indispensable implementation left unfinished by oversized scope.

candidates.reason: The required deliverable was already placed in /output and artifact validation succeeded; no complete candidate waited unpromoted or unpackaged before closure.
There is no evidence that a child implementation was merged after integrated verification; verification ran after agent-0's implementation was available.
The completed implementation child result was returned, spot-checked by the parent, copied as the artifact, and passed official evaluation.
No completed verifier finding is shown trapped below the parent; completed verifier summaries reached the aggregate result, while the unfinished verifier is covered by Early Child Termination.
The only child failure was the cancelled verifier in the retained timing episode; no separate required implementation failure needed takeover before artifact success.
The parent consumed agent-0's completed result and no completed verifier result is shown available at a later decision point and ignored inconsistently.
The parent blocked on the swarm call and the concrete event is child cancellation at timeout; no separate available progress was parent-visible and ignored during a wait.
No concurrent agents wrote competing implementation paths; agent-0 owned implementation and verifier agents read the finished executable.
No two live agents edited the same source file and no reconciliation of another live edit is visible.
No agent replaced non-entry source owned by another live agent; observed source edits were within the implementation child.
The final executable and test16.rs were not overwritten by competing live owners; the implementation child built the deliverable and verifiers read it.
No cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs from another agent in the final workspace.
The shared /output workspace was used, but only one child wrote implementation files and no unstable provenance problem is evidenced.
No generated fixture, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed as a stable reference by another actor.
